summary: This note presents Hawkwing Inc.'s Professional Development Policy, which sets guidelines for employee skill development in line with career goals and company objectives. It covers the types of opportunities, eligibility, a four-step in-house training procedure, and support for external courses and conferences. It also covers skill refreshers every two years and the compliance responsibilities of employees, department heads and HR.
one_line: Hawkwing Inc.'s Professional Development Policy outlines eligibility, in-house training steps, external course approval, skill refreshers and compliance responsibilities.
key_facts: Hawkwing Inc.'s Professional Development Policy aims to give employees a systematic, accessible approach to skill development aligned with career goals and strategic company objectives.

Development opportunities include job-specific training, leadership and management programs, technical skills workshops, soft skills enhancement, cross-functional team training, and industry-related conferences and seminars.
Every full-time employee at Hawkwing Inc. is eligible for professional development programs after completing six months of service.
Part-time employees at Hawkwing Inc. may be considered based on departmental discretion and availability of resources.
In-house training Step 1 is identifying training needs, done with supervisors and facilitated by annual performance reviews and personal development planning sessions.
In Step 2, employees consult the Hawkwing Inc. Training Calendar and register for in-house sessions through the internal training portal or the HR department.
In-house sessions can be workshops, webinars, or peer-led training, and employees are expected to actively engage and apply learned skills in their roles.
After training, participants are required to give feedback so HR and the Training Department can improve future offerings, and supervisors follow up to support implementation.
External courses and conferences are encouraged, with time off approval and potential financial assistance subject to policy guidelines and budget availability.

The external request process: submit a formal request to your supervisor, await department-head approval considering budget and operational needs, then coordinate with HR for registration and funding.
Employees are advised to revisit their skills every two years and take refresher or advanced training through the professional development program.
Department heads and HR monitor policy compliance and facilitate resources, while each employee is responsible for actively pursuing their own development.
